page.overview:
What is Assamite Schism?

The Assamite Schism is a civil strife, bordering civil war, within Clan Assamite. The Ashirra hunters and Preservationist Assamites ally with the Camarilla against Ur-Shulgi-led Path of Blood ancient fanatics. The Sabbat-aligned Assamite antitribu defend their beliefs against Haqim, although some have suspended their convictions and joined the Shepherds of Ur-Shulgi.

The Assamite clan had a diversity that Western Kindred never suspected. Following the removal of the Tremere curse by Ur-Shulgi's awakening, Kindred started seeing evidence of great turmoil building within the clan. Assamites take clan identity more seriously than most Kindred, so they take their differences seriously too. The Tremere curse held the clan together through shared resentment and the trade in vitae. With that external pressure removed, they can no longer paper over their disagreements.

Religions run like a great schasm through the Assamite clan. Most Assamites come from Muslim countries, with minorities of Zoroastrians, Jews, Eastern Christians, Baha'i and related religions. The most ancient Methuselahs of the clan however, remember time before all those religions. The Assamites have tried to compromise between mortal religion and the Path of Blood, casting their Antediluvian as a wrathful prophet in the line reaching from Adam to Mohammed. As the clan's true elders awaken, however, their deputies realize that their grandsires are a bunch of "devilish heathens." Ur-Shulgi, Haqim's childe and returned Master of Alamut, is not a servant of Allah. Many Assamites readily accept diablerie and war against all other vampires as their only creed. Like so many mortals, they mouth whatever dogma serves their purpose while their true gods remain Obedience, Ambition and Appetite. As the Methuselahs insist that the clan return to the old gods and the pure form of the Path of Blood, however, increasing numbers of younger Assamites bridle at such "paganism." They can accept Haqim as their prophet, but not as their god.

The Assamites also differ in their response to the end of the Tremere curse. The followers of the Path of Blood view diablerie as a sacrament. They believe that the incredible rush of consumming another vampire's soul is the touch of Haqim's divine grace. Other Assamites, trained for decades or centuries in rigid honor, see the lust for vitae for what it is: an addiction. The loss of self-control horrifies them. Both sides can justify their position through faith. Exceptionally devout Muslims argue that Islam's prohibition against drunkenness forbids all forms of intoxication, including diablerie. More moderate Assamites make an exception for the kalif drug used by the clan's blood-sorcerers. These Assamites want the clan to continue collecting vitae for generation-reducing potions. A few Assamites feel such disgust for their addiction that they see monastic seclusion from other vampires as the only escape from temptation. They renounce even artificial diablerie. Path of Blood devotees retort that the addictive pleasure of vitae is God's way of encouraging them to diablerize the wicked vampires of other clans.
